principles: cli-engine.ts remains the compatibility facade for public/test-facing symbols.
Catalog, schemas, and future parser/runtime/lifecycle slices must stay mechanically separated.
Focused smoke tests should compare command identity and representative help instead of trusting build alone.
drivers: cli-engine.ts is a high-risk god file with many gate-facing command definitions.
Existing tests import MAIN_TOOLS from cli-engine.ts.
Sibling stories will later move flags/help/runtime/lifecycle surfaces and need a stable catalog boundary first.

options.name: A: Extract catalog/schema modules with compatibility re-export
pros: Preserves existing import path for MAIN_TOOLS and ToolDef
Creates stable boundary for later parser/runtime/lifecycle stories
cons: Requires moving a large block carefully
New module still imports many schema prompt constants

options.name: B: Leave MAIN_TOOLS in cli-engine and add only helper wrappers
cons: Does not materially split the god file
Does not unblock later story dependencies

options.name: C: Move handlers and catalog together
pros: Larger architectural cleanup in one pass

chosen: A: Extract catalog/schema modules with compatibility re-export
rationale: Choose the narrow extraction because it delivers real cli-engine size reduction while preserving the command contract and leaving parser/runtime/lifecycle work to sibling stories.

preMortem.scenario: A schema describe/default/enum changes during the move.
preMortem.trigger: Manual copy misses a helper or imports a different Zod type.
preMortem.consequence: CLI help or argument validation changes silently.
preMortem.mitigation: Run build plus command catalog smoke comparing representative command names and help output.

preMortem.scenario: Existing tests importing MAIN_TOOLS from cli-engine break.
preMortem.trigger: MAIN_TOOLS is moved without a compatibility export.
preMortem.consequence: Downstream smoke tests fail and public surface regresses.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep ToolDef and MAIN_TOOLS exported from cli-engine.ts and add smoke coverage.

preMortem.scenario: The story expands into flag parser/help/runtime code.
preMortem.consequence: Parallel sibling stories conflict and review scope fails.
preMortem.mitigation: Only move schema/catalog definitions; leave parseFlags/help/runCli/root gates in cli-engine.ts.
